Completed Deliverable: Vendor Contract Renewal

Amusement and Recreation • Kingstree Partners • Media rights negotiation support phase • Archived 1993-12-18

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's media rights negotiation support phase engagement with Kingstree Partners in the Amusement and Recreation sector. The record ID 27288c22 uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • Analysis of Kingstree Partners's corporate venture capital arm found that its investments have a 13% follow-on funding rate, trailing the Amusement and Recreation benchmark and suggesting a need to refine its investment thesis.
  • The current director compensation program places total board member pay at the 10th percentile, but the equity component is 13% below the median, suggesting a rebalancing is needed to enhance director-shareholder alignment.
  • Compensation committee assessment framework benchmarking identified 135 process enhancements aligned with emerging market practice and activist investor expectations.
  • Long-term incentive grant date fair value benchmarking placed median Kingstree Partners executive grants at the 75th percentile of the 52-company peer group on a grant-date-FMV basis.
  • ESG metric integration analysis evaluated 223 potential environmental, social, and governance measures for potential inclusion in the annual or long-term incentive program design.
  • Our analysis of Kingstree Partners's business continuity plan showed that the recovery time objective for 133 critical applications is 36 hours, failing to meet the business requirement of 4 hours.
Key Findings
  • Text analysis of 140 Amusement and Recreation sector job postings scraped during the media rights negotiation support identifies a 28% increase in the prevalence of explicit pay range disclosure relative to the 1993 baseline, with Kingstree Partners's current job posting practices benchmarking at the 140th percentile of a 28-company peer set on transparency completeness.
  • The skills gap analysis conducted during the media rights negotiation support for Kingstree Partners identified 20 critical skill deficiencies across 4 functional domains, with the largest gaps concentrated in data literacy, agile delivery, and human-centered design — skills increasingly central to competitive positioning in the Amusement and Recreation sector as of 1993-12-18.
  • Latent class analysis applied to the Amusement and Recreation sector survey dataset (n=122) identifies 17 distinct governance archetypes, each with characteristic profiles on lost time injury rate, board composition, and executive pay structure. Kingstree Partners's archetype assignment and its strategic implications are detailed in the media rights negotiation support supporting appendix.
  • Labor cost benchmarking conducted during the media rights negotiation support for Kingstree Partners reveals that labor as a percentage of revenue is 199% above the Amusement and Recreation sector median across 35 comparable operating units, with the excess concentrated in management layers rather than hourly workforce costs — consistent with a span-of-control ratio of 199:1 against a market median of 35:1.

Our competitive assessment found that Kingstree Partners's compensation for mission-critical technology roles trails the Amusement and Recreation market by 14%, creating a significant hiring and retention risk that requires immediate attention.

ACPWB's media rights negotiation support assessment of Kingstree Partners's long-term incentive program evaluated plan design, performance metric selection, payout leverage, and competitive positioning across 240 dimensions. Drawing on data from 12 Amusement and Recreation sector peers benchmarked as of 1993-12-18, the analysis produced 240 design alternatives reviewed by the compensation committee.

ACPWB's media rights negotiation support analysis of Amusement and Recreation sector talent market dynamics identified 237 emerging workforce trends with material implications for Kingstree Partners's total rewards strategy. The findings, covering 38 talent pools across 237 functional specializations, were presented to Kingstree Partners's CHRO and compensation committee on 1993-12-18.

ACPWB's media rights negotiation support spans-and-layers analysis for Kingstree Partners examined management structure across 17 organizational levels in the Amusement and Recreation sector. The engagement identified 9 delayering opportunities and a structural redesign that reduces management cost by approximately 17% while maintaining or improving decision velocity, as reviewed by Kingstree Partners's executive committee on 1993-12-18.

ACPWB's media rights negotiation support analysis of Amusement and Recreation sector workforce cost structures identified 148 cost driver categories with material benchmarking implications for Kingstree Partners. The analysis drew on proprietary data from 27 comparable organizations and informed a total workforce cost optimization initiative projected to achieve a 148% cost reduction over 27 years.
